story.title: Experience shaped our purpose
story.imageAlt: Technician programming a flat knitting machine threaded with magenta and blue yarn

items.label: 20 years ago
items.text: Our story began with Funky Treko, our knitwear factory in Salamoun El-Qamash, Dakahlia, Egypt.

items.label: What caught our attention
items.text: Working with many brands across local and international markets, we kept facing the same problem: fragmented suppliers, inconsistent quality, limited visibility, and no single party accountable for the complete journey. Clients felt lost in the complexity of manufacturing and timelines, often unsure exactly what they needed.

items.label: The gap
items.text: No one owning the full journey on the client's side.

items.label: 2019 · Apparate is founded
items.text: To close that gap, Apparate brought manufacturing expertise, production management, rigorous quality assurance, and transparent client guidance together through one accountable team.

stages.title: Project onboarding
stages.text: Understand the client, market, quantity, and expectations.

stages.title: Project brief & feasibility
stages.text: Review construction, materials, quality, timing, and suitability.

stages.title: Costing & order confirmation
stages.text: Define commercial scope, responsibilities, approvals, and plan.

stages.title: Development & sample approval
stages.text: Confirm the approved product standard before bulk production.

stages.title: Pre-production & release
stages.text: Verify materials, measurements, trims, branding, packing, and approvals.

stages.text: Coordinate manufacturing, inspections, visibility, and corrective action.

timelines.title: Clear working timelines
notes: Bulk-production timing begins after the required pre-production approvals and materials are confirmed.
Each timeline is confirmed after reviewing complexity, fabric and trim availability, quantity, finishing, manufacturing allocation, sample requirements, and approval timing.

items.title: Sample inspection
items.text: The sample is checked against the pattern and the brief: measurements, materials, construction, trims, branding, and finishing.

items.title: First-piece inspection
items.text: The first piece entering the production line is checked progressively at relevant stages to confirm the approved requirements transfer correctly.

items.title: Inline quality control
items.text: While production is running, work in progress is tested to detect and fix errors at the earliest stage: recurring defects, measurement variation, construction, and finishing.

items.title: Final quality inspection
items.text: The completed order is checked for workmanship, appearance, quantities, branding, finishing, and packing.

standards.title: The standard stays visible
standards.text: Final QC follows international quality standards (AQL), agreed with every client.

levels.label: Critical defects
levels.text: Safety or regulatory failures, such as a stray needle or an unsafe sharp component.

levels.label: Major defects
levels.text: Defects that reduce usability, such as open seams, fabric holes, or broken stitches.

levels.label: Minor defects
levels.text: Small finishing defects that do not affect use, such as loose threads.

controls: Measurement, tolerances, fabric, shade and GSM checks
Branding placement and needle or metal detection where required
standards.note: Production acceptance is based on approved samples and documented inspections.

items.a: Apparate is an end-to-end apparel manufacturing and quality-assurance partner based in Egypt. We manage the full journey for local and regional brands, from brief and feasibility to sampling, bulk production, quality control and delivery, through one accountable team.

items.q: What is your minimum order quantity?
items.a: Our minimum order is 100 pieces per color. Final minimums are confirmed in a project-specific feasibility review, because materials, trims and construction can affect them.

items.q: How many pieces can you produce per month?
items.a: Up to 50,000 pieces per month across a network of 50+ specialized production partners. Capacity and factory allocation are confirmed for each project.

items.q: How long do sampling and bulk production take?
items.a: An initial sample takes about 5 working days and a pre-production sample about 3 working days. Standard bulk production takes about 4 weeks, and about 5 weeks in peak season. Bulk timing starts after pre-production approvals and materials are confirmed.

items.q: What quality standards do you inspect to?
items.a: Every order passes four quality gates: sample inspection, first-piece inspection, inline QC at 10–20% of production, and final inspection. Final QC follows AQL standards agreed with the client: zero acceptance for critical defects, AQL 2.5 for major defects and AQL 4.0 for minor defects.

items.q: Which printing and embroidery techniques do you offer?
items.a: Printing: DTF, DTG, rubber, vinyl (including silver reflective and glitter), sublimation, silicone and silk screen with up to 10 colors. Embroidery: flat, 3D puff, appliqué, patches, chenille, sequins and specialty threads. Techniques can be combined in one product.
Sportswear, knitwear, everyday and lifestyle wear, outerwear, baby and kidswear, and scarves and textile accessories such as printed scarves and tote bags, across knitted, woven and denim fabrics.

items.q: Do you work with clients in Saudi Arabia and the GCC?
items.a: Yes. For regional clients we manage production and quality oversight in Egypt through FOB handover, with licensed partners handling export documentation, customs, freight and shipping. High-volume Saudi and GCC shipments are expected to move mainly by sea, with Sokhna and Safaga as potential ports.

items.q: How do I start a project with Apparate?
items.a: Share your product reference or tech pack, quantity and colors, fabric, printing or embroidery, accessories, target delivery date and destination. An experienced apparel account manager reviews the brief, identifies the manufacturing and sourcing route, highlights key risks and confirms the next step.
